parts.label: a
parts.technique: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
parts.reason: S5.1 covers hypothesis testing developed through correlation coefficients but explicitly states 'calculation of correlation coefficients is excluded' and restricts calculation to the PMCC via calculator, not a formula. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient and the ranking/tied-ranks method used here is a distinct named technique that no statement mentions at all, so it is out regardless of the arithmetic similarity to S2.3.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for correlation using Spearman's coefficient
parts.reason: This part uses the answer from (a) (Spearman's rs) and tests it against a critical value; S5.1 only covers hypothesis testing for the PMCC (denoted ρ, tested against ρ=0), not Spearman's rank correlation, which is a separate named technique not mentioned in any statement. It also depends on the out-of-spec part (a).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sample mean calculation for goodness-of-fit test of Poisson model
parts.reason: This calculates a mean from a frequency table (superficially like S2.3), but it is explicitly set up as a step in testing suitability of a Poisson distribution. Poisson distribution is not named in any statement (only binomial and Normal distributions are covered in S4.1/S4.2), so any part relying on it is out regardless of the arithmetic involved.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Poisson expected frequencies
parts.reason: Requires understanding of expected frequencies generated from a Poisson probability model; Poisson is not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement, so this is out.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Combining cells for chi-squared goodness-of-fit test
parts.reason: This is part of setting up a chi-squared goodness-of-fit test (requiring expected frequencies >5), a technique not mentioned in any statement (only binomial proportion test, normal mean test, and correlation-based tests appear in Section 5).

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test for Poisson distribution
parts.reason: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit testing and the Poisson distribution are not covered by any statement; S5 only covers hypothesis tests for a binomial proportion (S5.2) and for a Normal mean (S5.3), with correlation coefficients in S5.1. This whole part is out.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Unbiased estimates of population mean and variance from summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculating standard deviation (and hence variance) from summary statistics using Sxx, and calculation of the mean is standard. No named exclusion applies to 'unbiased estimator' terminology; the calculation performed (p = sum x / n, q from Sxx/(n-1)) is the same technique as S2.3 applied to sample data, just with different labelling/divisor convention, which the specification itself acknowledges as acceptable.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Two-sample z-test for difference of population means with known/estimated variances
parts.reason: S5.3 only covers a hypothesis test for the mean of a single Normal distribution with known/given/assumed variance; a two-sample test comparing means of two independent populations is a distinct, more advanced technique not described by any statement, so it is out.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Justification via Central Limit Theorem for large samples
parts.reason: S5.3 explicitly states 'Knowledge of the Central Limit Theorem or other large sample approximations is not required', and this part directly requires that concept to justify normality of sample means; it also depends on the out-of-spec two-sample test in (b).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Confidence interval for a Normal mean - standard error derivation
parts.reason: Confidence intervals are not mentioned as a topic in any 9MA0 statement (Section 5 covers only hypothesis testing for a binomial proportion and for a Normal mean, not confidence intervals). This entire topic is absent from the specification.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: 95% confidence interval for a Normal mean
parts.reason: Confidence intervals are not covered by any statement; also depends on the out-of-spec standard error found in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding confidence level from interval width
parts.reason: Confidence intervals are not covered by any statement and this part depends on results from (a) and (b).

parts.label: a(i)
parts.technique: Advantages of quota sampling
parts.reason: S1.1 explicitly states students should be familiar with quota sampling and be able to comment on advantages/disadvantages of sampling techniques.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.technique: Disadvantages of quota sampling
parts.reason: S1.1 explicitly covers quota sampling and critiquing sampling techniques including disadvantages.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Expected frequencies for a contingency table (chi-squared test set-up)
parts.reason: This is a preparatory calculation for a chi-squared test of independence, a technique not named or described in any statement; Section 5 only covers binomial proportion tests, Normal mean tests, and correlation coefficient tests.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Chi-squared test of independence for a contingency table
parts.reason: Chi-squared tests of independence/association are not mentioned in any statement; S5.1-S5.3 cover only correlation coefficient tests, binomial proportion tests, and Normal mean tests, so this is out.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Bias of an estimator based on the continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: The continuous uniform distribution is not named or described in any statement (S4.1 covers only discrete distributions, explicitly excluding mean/variance calculation for general discrete random variables, and S4.2 covers only the Normal distribution among continuous distributions, excluding pdf knowledge). Bias of an estimator is also not a named concept in any statement.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Bias of an estimator
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec result from (a) and continues use of the continuous uniform distribution and bias concept, neither of which is covered by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Constructing an unbiased estimator
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec continuous uniform distribution and bias concepts from (a)/(b), none of which are covered by any statement.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Point estimation using sample mean for continuous uniform distribution parameter
parts.reason: Relies on the continuous uniform distribution and the estimator constructed in (c), neither of which is in the specification.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Distribution of a linear combination (sum) of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: S4.2 covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution as a model but does not mention combining independent Normal random variables (sums with combined mean/variance); this is a distinct technique not described by any statement.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Distribution of the difference of two independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: As with (a), forming and using the distribution of a difference of two independent Normal variables is not mentioned in S4.2 or any other statement, so this is out.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Distribution of a linear combination of Normal random variables with unknown n, solved via a resulting quadratic
parts.reason: This requires forming the distribution of a general linear combination of n+1 Normal random variables, a technique beyond simply 'finding probabilities using the Normal distribution' (S4.2); it is not described by any statement.
